headline: Microsoft has delayed to 1 December its plan to bill new Copilot Business subscriptions by usage by default, and has added a default monthly spending limit.
score_reason: Pool score kept: it changes what small businesses and their IT resellers may pay for AI tools, though it is a delay of a plan already known, not a new policy.
importance_line: Small-business customers and the IT resellers who must pay any unexpected charges get about a month more and a default spending limit before pay-per-use AI billing starts, but the plan is going ahead and Microsoft did not name the markets where it begins.
summary: CRN reports that Microsoft has pushed the start of default pay-per-use billing for new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions sold through its reseller partners from 2 Nov to 1 Dec 2026. Microsoft also set a default limit of 4,000 usage credits (about $40) per user each month, which resellers can change or set to zero, and a list of eleven countries, including Germany, France and India, where the billing will not start at first.
notes: Follow-up of the 1 Oct 2026 CRN story on Microsoft turning this billing on by default. Date of the delay announcement is not stated; the article mentions Microsoft document updates on 30 Sep and 1 Oct 2026, so the score was not lowered.
